J U D G M E N T
The plaintiff has filed this suit as against the defendant seeking the relief of permanent injunction for costs and for such other further reliefs.

2. Brief facts of the plaintiff's case is as follows:-
That the plaintiff is the wife of defendant and their marriage took place on 11.06.1995 as per Hindu Rites and Customs.
After the marriage they are started to reside together in the address shown in the plaint cause title i.e., in the suit schedule property as husband and wife.
Out of the said wedlock the plaintiff had gave birth to two children namely Nataraja S. now aged about 26 years and Niveditha S. who is now 22 years.
The plaintiff is having ration card, Aadhaar card, PAN card for the above address.

She is paying electricity bills to the BESCOM in respect of O.S.
No.25066/2023 the suit schedule property.

The plaintiff and defendant have lead marital life only for few years and thereafter some misunderstanding arose between them and defendant has filed M.C.No.3969/2012 before the IV Addl. Principal Family Court Judge, Bengaluru against the plaintiff seeking the relief of divorce.

entities.text: IV Addl. Principal Family Court Judge, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The said case was dismissed on the ground that the defendant herein not proved his case.
Thereafter, the defendant herein has not preferred any appeal challenging the said Judgment and decree.

The plaintiff also filed a criminal case in C.C.No.18956/2013 against the defendant for offence punishable u/sec.498A, 323, 504 and 506 of IPC Drakshayini vs M Somashekar Murthy on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143277401/
2 and in the said case the defendant was acquitted.

sentences.text: 3. According to plaintiff the family of the plaintiff and defendant inherited some landed properties from their O.S. No.25066/2023 ancestors and they are joint family members and out of the income of said property the suit property and other property were acquired.

There was oral partition between the family members of the predecessors of plaintiff and defendant and accordingly,
respective sharers were put in their respective shares.

Subsequently, partition was held between defendant, his father, brother and mother under the registered partition deed dated 01.12.2006 and as per the said partition deed the suit property was allotted to the share of defendant.
The plaintiff being wife of the defendant is residing in the suit property along with her children and the defendant is making attempt to dispossess the plaintiff and children from the suit property.

The plaintiff being wife is having right over the residential house in the suit property to stay in the house and to O.S.
No.25066/2023 enjoy the same.
On 10.01.2023 at about 10.30am the defendant tried to dispossess the plaintiff from the suit property.
The defendant brought real estate agent for negotiation to sell the suit property.
The plaintiff enquired in this regard and at that time the defendant given evasive answer.
Accordingly, the plaintiff has filed this suit and prays to decree the suit.

4. After registration of this suit the suit summons was came to be issued to the defendant and the same returned as un-claimed and hence the defendant was placed exparte and the case was posted for plaintiffs' evidence.
5. That to prove the case of the plaintiff she herself got examined as P.W.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.22 documents.
Heard the arguments.
Perused the pleadings, evidence, documents and available materials placed on record.

7. Following points arisen for my consideration are:
1. Whether the plaintiff proves her lawful possession over the suit property as on the date of suit?
2. whether the plaintiff proves the alleged interference by the defendant?
3. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for suit relief as prayed for?
4. What order or decree?
8. My findings to above points are as under:-
Point No.1 : In the negative Point No.2 : In the negative Point No.3 : In the negative Point No.4 : As per the final order for the following:-
Drakshayini vs M Somashekar Murthy on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143277401/
3 O.S. No.25066/2023 R E A S O N S 9.
POINT No.1 & 2:- These points are interrelated and connected to each other, to avoid repetition, I have taken them together for discussion.
10. It is the specific case of the plaintiff that she is wife of defendant and their marriage was held on 11.06.1995 as per Hindu Rites and Customs.
Out of their wedlock they are having two children, the plaintiff is residing in suit schedule property by obtaining necessary electricity connection, water connection and gas cylinder connection.

It is only for few years they have lead happy marital life and thereafter some misunderstanding arose between them and defendant has filed M.C.No.3969/2012 before the IV Addl. Principal Family Court Judge against the plaintiff seeking the relief of divorce and the said case O.S. No.25066/2023 was came to be dismissed.
The plaintiff also filed a criminal case in C.C.No.18956/2013 against the defendant for offence punishable u/sec.498A, 323, 504 and 506 of IPC and in the said case the defendant has been acquitted.
The defendant acquired the suit schedule property under the registered family partition deed dated 01.12.2006.
The plaintiff being wife is having right interest and possession over the residential house existing in the suit property.
The defendant is trying to dispossess the plaintiff and her children from the suit schedule property house.

11. The plaintiff in order to prove her case got examined herself as PW.1 and during the course of evidence she filed her chief examination affidavit reiterating the plaint averments, the plaintiff has produced 22 documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P22.
Ex.P1 is the marriage invitation, Ex.P2 is the partition deed dated 01.12.2006, Ex.P3 to 10 are the 8 receipts of LPG Gas, Ex.P11 to 17 are the 7 electricity bills, Ex
.P18 and 19 Aadhaar card of plaintiff and her daughter, Ex.P20 is the election ID card, Ex.P21 is the ration card and Ex.P22 is the notice issued by the BWSSB dated 2.12.2020.

13 . In the case on hand it is the case of the plaintiff that suit schedule property was allotted to the share of defendant under the registered partition deed dated 01.12.2006 which was effected in between the defendant, his father, brother and mother.

On perusal of Ex.P2 the copy of registered partition deed dated 01.12.2006 it shows that Mutthunarasimhaiah and his wife Puttachannamma as well as their children M.Nagraj, M.Somashekara Murthy got O.S. No.25066/2023 divided their family properties.
The defendant M.Somashekara Murthy was allotted with 'C' schedule which consist of 3 items.
The suit schedule property is bearing No.14 khatha No.148 formed out of survey No.65 with house list No.330/1.
The plaintiff has produced Gas connection receipts, electricity consumption bills.
The documents relied on by the plaintiff shows that the plaintiff is the wife of defendant and she is living in the house which stands in the name of Arasamma.
The electricity bills shows the name of Arasamma.
The plaintiff has not furnished any document which shows her name as person in possession of suit schedule property.
The plaintiff has not even produced any document which shows that she is in possession of suit schedule property.

The gas connection bills are raised in the name of plaintiff but the address O.S. No.25066/2023 shown in the said receipts does not Drakshayini vs M Somashekar Murthy on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143277401/
4 tally with the suit schedule property.
14. It is pertinent to note that as pleaded by the plaintiff herself the suit schedule property was allotted to the share of defendant.
The defendant is owner of the suit schedule property.
The plaintiff no doubt is wife of defendant.
However, it is necessary to note that the plaintiff is seeking the relief of permanent injunction as against the defendant.
As discussed above the defendant is owner of suit schedule property and the plaintiff being the wife of defendant can have right of maintenance and right of residence.
In the case on hand she is not seeking any such right of maintenance or right to reside in the suit schedule property.
On the contrary she is seeking the relief of permanent injunction as against the true owner i.e., O.S. No.25066/2023 defendant.
The plaintiff even if she is considered as co- owner of suit schedule property she cannot seek the relief of permanent injunction as against another co-owner.
Since the defendant is the owner of the suit schedule property the plaintiff being wife she cannot claim the relief of injunction against the true owner.
Accordingly, the plaintiff failed to establish her lawful possession over the suit schedule property.
The plaintiff also not produced any oral or documentary evidence to prove the alleged interference by the defendant.

15. The counsel for plaintiff has relied upon the decisions reported in ILR 2021 KAR 1642 (Sri.
S.B.Sampat Kumar Vs. Sri. S.B.Parasmal & another) wherein it is held as follows:
In the context of section 14(1) of the Act, legally speaking, pre-existing right can be said to be a right O.S. No.25066/2023 possessed by a woman to lay claim on the entire or part of the property, it may include right to inherit the property by birth as in the case of Hindu coparceners, a right to succeed to self acquisition properties of a male Hindu and right to claim maintenance also.
16.

entities.text:
ILR 2021 KAR 1642 (Sri.
S.B.Sampat Kumar Vs. Sri. S.B.Parasmal & another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have gone through the dictum laid down in the above case.
The present suit is filed seeking the relief of permanent injunction.
The plaintiff is not seeking the pre- existing right.

The defendant who is her husband is still alive and the suit property is acquired by husband under the partition deed i.e., Ex.P2 hence with due respect to the dictum the same will not assist the plaintiff.

17. The plaintiff also relied upon Judgment reported in AIR 2021 SC 177 Smt. S.Vanitha Vs. Deputy Commissioner, Bengaluru Urban District and Ors. and 2021 (1) KCCR SN 18 (SC) Sathish Chander Ahuja Vs.Sneha Ahuja O.S. No.25066/2023 18.

entities.text: AIR 2021 SC 177 Smt. S.Vanitha Vs. Deputy Commissioner, Bengaluru Urban District and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sathish Chander Ahuja Vs.Sneha Ahuja O.S. No.25066/2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have gone through the above decisions and with due respect to the principles the same are also not applicable to the facts and circumstances to the case on hand.
In the case on hand the plaintiff is seeking the relief of permanent injunction to restrain the defendant who is true owner of the suit schedule property from interfering with her possession.
Accordingly, the decisions relied on by the plaintiff are not applicable to the facts on hand.
Hence, the above decisions will not help the plaintiff.
The plaintiff has not made out her lawful possession over the suit schedule property as on the date of suit.
The plaintiff also failed to prove the alleged interference by the defendant.
Hence, I have answered Point No.1 and 2 in the negative.

sentences.text: 5 19. POINT No.3:-
In view of my findings on point No.1 and 2 which are held in the negative the plaintiff is not entitled for the suit relief as prayed for.
Hence, I have answered Point No.3 in the negative.
20. POINT No.4:-

For the reasons discussed in point Nos.1 to 3 and findings given on it by me, I proceed to pass the following:-
O R D E R
The suit filed by the plaintiff against the defendant is hereby dismissed.

No order as to costs.
Draw decree accordingly.
